contract: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are ordered crystal structures {'lattice': 3x3 lattice vectors as rows (Angstrom), 'species': element symbols, 'frac_coords': fractional coordinates per site}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and RDKit are importable (pandas and torch only where the environment provides them; they are not requirements of the task); wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric
notes: Official Matbench v0.1 data (SHA-256 equal to matminer's recorded hashes) and folds; structures are passed as plain lattice, species and fractional coordinates instead of pymatgen objects. Reference check: rescoring the stored predictions of AMMExpress v2020 and RF-SCM/Magpie reproduces their leaderboard MAEs exactly.

name: Matbench: refractive index of inorganic crystals
description: Predict the DFT refractive index of 4764 inorganic crystals from their structure. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.
benchmark: Matbench: refractive index of inorganic crystals
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Petousis et al. (2017): high-throughput DFPT screening of inorganic compounds for dielectric and optical materials; source of the targets.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Targets are DFT (DFPT) refractive indices with a few extreme values (up to 62) that dominate fold maxima; Materials Project data retrieved in 2019.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.
